Quotable Stephen Carmel U S Maritime Administrator Stephen Carmel did not – as many in this industry have – grow up with ‘saltwater in his veins ’ Carmel is a long-tenured and well-respected maritime industry executive and a leading voice driving the U S maritime rebuild but he grew up in a small Pennsylvania mountain town “Have you ever seen the movie The Deer Hunter? ” he asked “The Deer Hunter could have been shot in my hometown: a 10-square block town with a steel mill in the center and nothing but farmland around it The nearest McDonalds was 25 miles away!” His family didn’t have the money to send him away to college so he needed to find something for free: enter the United States Merchant Marine Academy He entered Kings Point at aged 17 and never looked back It was then that he took his first sea journey “I just fell in love with being at sea It's an experience that’s difficult to describe It's soul changing to be in the middle of the Pacific with a Milky Way blazing above you and understanding just how small you are Or watching the Northern Lights dance I mean it just changes who you are That’s when I said ‘all right this is it This is where I belong This is home So I graduated from Kings Point took my first ship and was gone for 15 months and I just couldn't imagine being anywhere else To me there was nothing more magical [than using a sextant] standing on the bridge looking at the stars and understanding where I was in the universe” Here are a collection of what we see as the best quotes from the U S Maritime Administrator when we corralled him for an hour plus interview in Chicago over the summer
• On competing with China "We cannot out-China the Chinese We can't beat the Chinese by being a cheaper version of China That's not how we're going to win We're going to win by changing the terms of competition We have a peer competitor that is absolutely focused on dominating the maritime space ”
• On American innovation "The U S is awesome at innovating at technology at disrupting That's what we're great at We have to make what the Chinese do irrelevant We need to stop inventing really cool stuff and walking away from it "
• On nuclear powered commercial shipping "SMR-powered nuclear technology will transform trade and shipping every bit as much — or more — than the container did "
• On rebuilding the U S Merchant Marine "We can't rebuild our industry with government cargo There's simply not enough of it We have to get back to carrying the nation's commerce "
• On America's biggest weakness "Our biggest weakness—our biggest challenge—is our own attitude We can revitalize our shipbuilding industry We can revitalize our maritime industry But we're not going to get there if we abandon the fight before we take the field "
• On America's future "A rich country is one that can build its own future "
• On urgency in addressing sealift and industrial capacity "We're out of time We have to quit fooling around and think that we can kick this can down the road "
• On the importance of the inland waterways "It does no good to build out this robust seacoast infrastructure if we've let the interior of the country fall apart "
